rows.40:65c8:
That the hands coming out of the pool weren't asking for help at all...
That maybe they were looking for the next person to drag under... that's what I think.
They say Hayashi set one school record after another before she graduated.
There were other girls who looked like they might set records too, but...
Apparently they all said the same thing.
When it really counted, something pulled at their legs and they couldn't swim right... they said.{p}
rows.40:671c:
Gives you chills, doesn't it?
Sure, just seeing Hayashi's figure wavering in the pool water with a hand reaching out of it isn't hard proof.
Maybe her reflection just happened to be on the water, and some ghost's hand or something came out of it, that's all.
But...
I'm going with the theory that it was Hayashi's living spirit.
Hey, {c}{f:|}, what do you think?{p}What do you think that figure of Hayashi wavering in the pool at night really was?
rows.40:6898: Hayashi was just reflected in the water
rows.40:68b0: It must have been Hayashi's living spirit
rows.40:68c8:
Huh?
Why would you say that?{p}
rows.40:6a68:
Right.
That's the only explanation, isn't it?
But if it wasn't...
Then maybe Hayashi had it a bit rough.
I mean...
The living-spirit theory about her got pretty famous.
And it seems she got harassed a lot because of it.
The girls who said something grabbed their legs in the pool and kept them from setting records were bullying her too.
It was pretty brutal, apparently.
Fights between girls can get scary{f:, you know.|, right?}
If the hand coming out of the pool was actually Seto's ghost...
Then Hayashi was framed for something she didn't do.
After her own death, Seto envied Hayashi for becoming the top of the swim club, and tormented her.
Then she got in the way of anyone who might set a record, too, and pinned it all on Hayashi...
Just kidding.
That's not it, right?
It's Hayashi's living spirit that's to blame, isn't it?
After all, you said so too, {c}{f:|}.
I bet everyone else thinks so too.
Well then, shall we move on to the next story?
Come on, whose turn is it next...?{p}
rows.40:6df4:
That's right.
More and more people started getting cramps in their legs while swimming.
And it was always someone swimming in Lane 4.
Lane 4 was the lane Seto used to swim in.
Our school's pool has eight lanes, right?
Apparently at swim meets, swimmers are placed from the center lanes outward, fastest times first.
Seto practiced in Lane 4 all the time, not just at meets.
And Lane 4 was where Seto died, too.
These days they call Lane 4 the Lane of Death and nobody will swim in it, but back then, the swim club members all dreamed of swimming in that lane.
They wanted to swim as fast and gracefully as Seto, so they practiced in Lane 4 like they were fighting over it.{p}
rows.40:7068:
Everyone could put up with a little leg cramp.
But after a while, it stopped being just leg cramps.{p}
rows.40:70f4:
The girl swimming in Lane 4 that day was named Hayashi; she'd been Seto's rival.
With Seto gone, she'd become the swim club's great hope, but her times just weren't improving.
So maybe she was hoping some of Seto's luck would rub off on her?
She went to the pool earlier than the other members and claimed Lane 4 for herself.{p}
rows.40:723c:
Hayashi swam alone, silently.
But after a while, she noticed something strange.{p}What was it...?
rows.40:72e0:
It was that someone was following behind her.
While she swam, she could see a figure at the edge of her vision.
She thought it was another member, but the figure seemed to be swimming in Lane 4.
I was here first!
Thinking that, she stopped to tell off whoever was coming up behind her.{p}
rows.40:749c:
"Huh, I must've imagined it."
This is where someone died, after all.
I'm just a little on edge, that's all.
She told herself that and started swimming again.{p}
rows.40:7534:
But as she swam, there it was again: someone's figure flickering in and out at the edge of her eye.
It's my imagination, just my imagination.
Hayashi kept swimming, muttering that to herself.
But soon she couldn't tell herself that anymore.
The figure was gradually getting closer.
The shadow she'd only glimpsed at the edge of her vision was now just one body length behind her!
And I haven't slowed my pace at all...
At this rate, it's going to catch me!{p}What should she do?★
rows.40:76d4: Pick up her pace and pull away
rows.40:76ec:
She must have been scared of whatever was coming up behind her, but she also had her pride as the swim club's great hope.
She picked up her pace, trying to pull away from the shadow in one burst.
And it seemed to work.
The shadow fell further and further behind.
But Hayashi didn't slow down one bit.
She was still uneasy, after all.
But no matter how long she fled, the unease wouldn't go away.
How far do I have to swim...?
The wall should be coming up soon...
The moment she thought that☆{p}
rows.40:78d0:
She saw that figure from before, right by her shoulder.
It was Seto.
Seto's graceful form, exactly the same as when she was alive.
Am I going to lose to Seto again?
Anything but that!
The instant she thought that...{p}
rows.40:79a4:
"Ow!☆"
Hayashi slammed full force into the pool wall.
She'd smashed her right arm, the one stroking through the water, straight into it.
As Hayashi's mind went blank with pain, Seto's voice rang in her ears.
"Oh, too bad.
The fish got away..."
That's what it said.{p}
rows.40:7ac4:
Hayashi's arm only had a cracked bone, and they said once it healed it wouldn't affect her swimming at all, but she was completely terrified.
In the end, she quit swimming.
They say she's married now, an ordinary housewife.
After Hayashi, three people went missing at that pool.
Every one of them had been practicing in Lane 4.
When you think about that, maybe Hayashi made the right choice.
It's a shame about all that talent, though.{p}
rows.40:7c5c:
I wonder what happened to the ones who went missing?
All there is to go on is
"The fish got away..."
those words of Seto's. Nothing else.
Maybe Seto ate them, or maybe they're being kept in a fish tank...
Either way, I don't think they're in this world anymore.{p}
rows.40:7d50:
Hee hee hee.
Your class has swimming in P.E. tomorrow, right, {c}{f:|}?
Whatever you do, don't swim in Lane 4.
Though if you're reeeally confident, I won't stop you.
Well, that's the end of my story.
If the seventh one doesn't show up, the next person will be the last, huh.{p}
rows.40:7e44:
On instinct, Hayashi ducked under the lane rope and escaped into the next lane.
It was close to a gamble.
There was no guarantee that whatever was chasing her would just keep swimming straight ahead.
Even so, she had a feeling she'd have a better chance than if she kept swimming where she was.
And that feeling was right.{p}
rows.40:7f70:
The thing closing in behind Hayashi kept going straight down Lane 4 at a terrifying speed.
Hayashi got a good look at it.{p}
rows.40:8010:
It was Seto!
Nothing like her graceful form when she was alive: the way she clawed at the water, splashing frantically with a desperate look on her face, made it seem like she was trying to escape from something.
Just like Hayashi a moment ago, right?
And then, as if chasing after Seto, a girl swam past.
Behind that girl came another, and behind that one, another...
A whole line of people swimming down Lane 4, one after another.
Hayashi thought:
Until a moment ago, I was in that line too.
Eventually that strange line disappeared from sight, but they say Hayashi never went near Lane 4 again.{p}
rows.40:8238:
"If I'd kept swimming like that, I'd have died just like Seto.
And I'd have ended up swimming forever as one of that line."
That's what Hayashi told the younger members when she graduated.
I wonder if those people are still swimming even now?
To escape from whatever's coming up behind them...
Never noticing that there's someone in the same situation in front of them, too... you know?
Next time you have swimming class, go check for yourself.
Though you'll be in big trouble if the teacher catches you in Lane 4.
If you're ready for that, why not?
That's the end of my story.
...The seventh one isn't coming, huh.
I guess the next person will be the last?{p}
rows.40:8478:
It was that someone was pulling at her legs.
At first, it just felt like something had brushed her leg.
Well, in a pool, about the only thing that could touch your legs is the rope dividing the lanes.
If you can't swim straight, you've probably brushed against it or gotten caught on it a few times, right?
Hayashi tried not to let it bother her, but something kept touching her legs, so she finally stopped.{p}
rows.40:8604:
Then she looked around, wondering what on earth kept touching her.
But there was nothing like that anywhere.
The lane ropes were lined up neatly and straight, and there wasn't so much as a pebble in the water.
Of course it was spotless.
After Seto's accident, everyone had scrubbed it from top to bottom.
"Maybe I really am touching the lane rope?"
That was the only explanation she could think of.{p}
rows.40:8790:
Hayashi pulled herself together and started swimming again.
Taking care to keep going straight...
But still, every time, something touched her legs.
This is strange; I should be swimming straight...
Suddenly afraid of what was behind her, she picked up her pace and swam, trying to get away from whatever it was.
If I can just make it to the wall...
Once I reach the wall, I can climb out of there.
It won't be able to follow me out onto the poolside.
That's what she thought as she hurried.{p}
rows.40:8930:
...The wall came into view.
Just a little more...
Just a little more and...
The instant she relaxed, just for a second...!{p}
rows.40:89b0: Something grabbed her ankle with incredible strength☆{p}
rows.40:89f0:
Startled, Hayashi struggled desperately to tear that something off.
The thing that had grabbed her ankle...{p}It was...?
rows.40:8aa0:
It was Seto!
Well, Seto's ghost, to be exact.
Seto, her face deathly pale, was clinging desperately to Hayashi's leg and wouldn't let go.
Seto tightened her grip, trying to drag Hayashi down under the water.
There was a horrible crack, and a searing pain shot through Hayashi's leg.{p}
rows.40:8bb8:
"Aaaaaaaaaaaaaah!☆"
Hayashi's scream echoed through the pool.
Seto kept pulling her without mercy.
Hayashi's body was already completely underwater; only her arms were beating at the surface.
"I'm sorry, Seto.
I'm sorry..."
She couldn't get the words out clearly, but Hayashi kept apologizing with all her might.
She kept on apologizing, on and on.
"I'm sorry...
I'm sorry..."{p}
rows.40:8d2c:
By the time the other members heard Hayashi's scream and came running to the poolside, Seto was gone, and Hayashi was just crying and apologizing, they say.
So nobody believed in Seto's ghost, but once they saw Hayashi's leg, they couldn't just brush it off.{p}
rows.40:8e28:
There was a bright red handprint clearly left on Hayashi's ankle.
And her leg was even broken, so she graduated without ever being able to swim again.
But why had Seto's ghost appeared...
And why was Hayashi apologizing? The club members never found out.{p}
rows.40:8f34:
It'd be simple if Hayashi had killed Seto.
Like I said before, Seto died of a heart attack.
She died in an instant, right in front of everyone.
So there was no way Hayashi could have killed her.
Unless she'd been putting a curse on her in secret... that is.
Now, this is my big sister's guess...
Maybe, somewhere in her heart, Hayashi hated Seto.
Not anything you could call a curse; more like hatred on an everyday level, you know?
She could never beat Seto, after all.
If only Seto weren't around...
She was probably always thinking at least that much, don't you think?{p}
rows.40:9168:
But one day, it actually happened.
Seto's sudden death.
Maybe it was her own fault.
Because she'd always been thinking, if only Seto weren't around...
On top of that, she'd neatly snatched up Seto's old place for herself.
That fanned Hayashi's guilt even more.
And that guilt of Hayashi's appeared in the shape of Seto.
In other words, touching her legs, dragging her underwater, all of it was the work of Hayashi's own guilt.
She was terrified of her own feelings.{p}
rows.40:9334:
...That's what my big sister thinks.
I think so too.
After Hayashi's incident, lots of people who swam in Lane 4 killed themselves, apparently.
They're fine before they swim, but afterwards they go white as a sheet, and
"I'm sorry..."
they mutter, wandering off somewhere in a daze.
The way they killed themselves was different each time, but their suicide notes always mention Seto, apparently.
I'm the one who killed Seto.
Supposedly the notes say something like that.
Even people who'd never met Seto wrote notes like that, so the school and the police were really stumped.
It's hard enough to believe that stuff about Hayashi's guilt, but people killing themselves because of it? There's no easy way to explain that, is there?
In the end, once they'd figured out the cause seemed to be Lane 4 of the pool, they banned Lane 4.
But no matter how strict they are, every year one or two students still get into Lane 4.
Well, that pool's getting pretty old, so maybe they'll tear it down and rebuild it?
I guess we just have to hang on till then?
...Okay, that's the end of my story.
If the seventh one doesn't show up, the next person will be the last, huh.{p}
rows.40:98b0:
The very next day, she apparently handed in a letter quitting the swim club.
Everyone wondered what on earth had happened.
She might have been in a slump, but Hayashi had been all fired up to work hard enough for Seto's sake too.
On top of that, Hayashi didn't just quit the swim club; she started skipping P.E., but only on swimming days.
Just like Seto, she'd loved being in the water, and if you left her alone, she wouldn't get out of the pool for hours...
It was as if she were scared of the pool and trying her hardest to stay away from it.
And then, right around when everyone had gotten used to Hayashi hating the pool...{p}
rows.40:9ad0:
Hayashi was found drowned.
In the school pool.
When the swim club members came for morning practice, Hayashi was floating in Lane 4 in her sailor uniform.
Why would she go to the very place she'd been avoiding so hard?
And why had she started avoiding it in the first place...{p}
rows.40:9bf8:
I heard this from my big sister: apparently Seto had gone through the same thing as Hayashi before.
While she was swimming alone, something pulled at her leg.
Supposedly she even showed people the handprint on her ankle.
It seems Hayashi was with her at the time.
And then Seto died right after that, right?
I bet Hayashi sensed that she was next.
That's why she quit the swim club and avoided the pool.
But in the end, she couldn't escape death after all.
What could it be, the thing that pulls you down from under the water?
The sports world is pretty cutthroat, you know.
People tend to think it's all so wholesome, but it has its ugly, murky side too.
I don't really understand it, but...
That ugly, murky human greed is lurking in Lane 4 of that pool.
It might look like clear water, but it's actually filthier and scarier than the bottom of a swamp.
And you could say the same about places that aren't pools, right?
It's hiding everywhere: in the gym, on the athletic field, anywhere.{p}
rows.40:9f6c:
Hee hee hee, P.E. is going to be a lot more fun from now on.
Your class has swimming tomorrow, as it happens, doesn't it, {c}{f:|}?
Don't you dare skip it.
...Just kidding.
Well, that's as far as my story goes.
I wonder what happened to the seventh one?
If they don't come, the next person is the last, huh.{p}
rows.40:a078:
It was that while she swam, she felt like someone was watching her.
...That's what it was.
She thought the other members had arrived, but when she looked around, there was nobody.
Hayashi was alone in the pool...{p}
rows.40:a1dc:
But sure enough, as she swam, she felt someone's eyes on her.
No, not now, with the meet coming up...
I have to focus harder.
Hayashi kept swimming, telling herself that.
...The human mind is a strange thing, isn't it?
When you think, I have to focus!
don't you end up thinking about all kinds of other stuff even more?
Concentrating your mind is really hard, isn't it?
It's probably different for people who do calligraphy or martial arts, but...
On a normal day, Hayashi wouldn't have let something like this throw her off, but she'd been worrying about her times.
The next meet was already spinning round and round in her head.
What if I can't win...?
I couldn't even beat Seto; can someone like me really take first place?
If I lose...★
Everyone will be so disappointed.
The younger members, the teachers, Mom and Dad...
Once gloomy thoughts get going, they're hard to stop, aren't they?
It's like you can't see the end of them.{p}
rows.40:a500:
Finally she stopped, and started crying in the middle of the pool.
She could've saved the crying for after she actually lost the meet, right?
But at that moment, she couldn't shake the feeling that she was completely worthless.
I wonder how long she cried...?
I don't think it was very long, but...
Then she heard people talking.{p}
rows.40:a650:
"Hey, that girl's crying."
"Ew, how pathetic."
Hayashi panicked.
She didn't want anyone to see her looking so miserable.
She quickly wiped her tears with her hand and put on a big smile.
It was a little forced, but it was the best smile she could manage.{p}
rows.40:a738:
But there was no one there.
There was nobody in the pool, or on the poolside.
Was I hearing things...?
But as if to deny that thought, she heard the voices again.{p}
rows.40:a800:
"Do you think she lost?"
"She did.
She couldn't win again."
"She just isn't ace material, is she?"
The voices took turns tearing Hayashi down.
Even Hayashi lost her temper at that, it seems.
She yelled at the top of her lungs.
"Who's there?!
Saying whatever you like...
Stop hiding and come out!"
Then the voices, which had been so noisy, suddenly went dead silent, they say.
And the next instant...!{p}
rows.40:a980:
Countless figures appeared all around Hayashi!
There were adults, children, women, and men.
In the pool, on the poolside, the whole place was overflowing with people.
Only their eyes glittered, every one of them, and they all stared hard at Hayashi.{p}
rows.40:ab10:
When Hayashi timidly raised her head, the people were gone, they say.
She couldn't hear the voices anymore, either.
...But even so, she still felt eyes on her.
Where from?
From above...
Not from the poolside...
Higher.
Higher than that...
Thinking that, she looked straight up above her.
And there...{p}
rows.40:ac48:
A single giant eyeball was staring down at Hayashi.
She couldn't move a muscle until it disappeared, they say.{p}
rows.40:acd8:
By the time the other swim club members gathered, the eyeball was gone, and Hayashi was just standing in the middle of the pool.
The other members didn't take Hayashi's story seriously.
But gradually, more members started hearing those voices or being surrounded by crowds of people, and they had no choice but to believe it.
It was always someone who'd been swimming in Lane 4 who went through it.
So Lane 4 was banned.
There was what happened to Seto, too, after all.{p}
rows.40:ae7c:
...Huh, Hayashi?
After this incident, she pulled herself right out of her slump, broke records at all kinds of meets, and then graduated.
Oh yeah, when she graduated, she said something like this to the younger members.
"I don't know exactly what it was I experienced in Lane 4, but maybe that's what happens when pressure takes on a form.
I wonder if Seto saw it too...?"
That's what she said.
Pressure, huh... Even the best athletes feel it at least once, don't they?
"I cracked under the pressure..."
You hear that one a lot, and on the other hand,
"Whoever puts more pressure on their opponent wins."
people say that too, right?
I don't know since when, but maybe the thing called pressure has latched onto Lane 4.
After all, Lane 4 is proof you're at the top.
That's how much pressure all those people were putting on it.{p}
rows.40:b184:
...Hee hee hee.
Your class is cleaning the pool for P.E. tomorrow, right, {c}{f:|}?
Sneak into Lane 4 and see.
Don't worry, there's no water in it, and you won't be swimming, so nothing's going to happen.
...Well, at most, everyone might stare at you, {c}{f:|}.
That won't make you feel any pressure, will it?
What counts is staying relaxed.
That's the end of my story, but... the seventh one still isn't here, huh.
I guess the next person will be the last...{p}
rows.40:b324:
Oh, come on.
You're actually curious, aren't you?
Hee hee, I'll take you there, just this once.
Let's go see.
Whether the cursed locker really exists.{p}
rows.40:b3b8:
Sure, we're not exactly going in with permission, so I get why you wouldn't want to.
But we just have to make sure nobody ever finds out.{p}Come on, let's go, let's go☆
